newsitem.title: INDIA: India NALCO raise prices of aluminium.
newsitem.headline: India NALCO raise prices of aluminium.

text.p: India's state-run National Aluminium Company (NALCO) said on Friday it had raised the prices of all grades of aluminium by 5,300 rupees per tonne.

"We have increased the prices of aluminium from April 2, but in principle it has not come into effect due to truckers strike," S.N. Johri, chairman of NALCO, told Reuters in the company's headquarters in the eastern city of Bhubaneshwar.

Truck owners launched an indefinite strike on Tuesday in protest against a five percent service tax on road transport which Finance Minister P. Chidambaram proposed in the federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March).
The protest has kept some 2.2 million trucks off the roads and crippled movement of goods and services.
NALCO, Asia's largest aluminium maker produced 203,650 tonnes of aluminium in 1996/97 (April-March) compared with 192,288 tonnes in 1995/96.
It has a market share of 35 percent.
